# 1: Project Overview

The goal of this project is to see how the rapid growth in AI data center power capacity coincide with growth in Canada's high-AI industries than its low-AI industries. The project through various data sources will visualize the variables contributing to this comparison.

## 2.2.1: Epoch AI Frontier Data Centers

**Producer and authority.** Epoch AI, an independent research institute founded in 2021 that
studies the trajectory of AI. No government mandate. It is a data-first research nonprofit investigating artificial intelligence.

**Original Dataset Purpose.** Built to track construction timelines of major AI data centers:
power capacity, compute capacity and capital cost over time. Not built to
measure electricity actually consumed.

**Collection method.** Estimated from high-resolution satellite imagery, permits and public
documents. The download includes reference tables of chillers (143 models)
and cooling towers (527 models), which Epoch uses to estimate a site's power
from the cooling equipment visible in satellite images. Epoch states 80%
confidence that a given power capacity is accurate.

**Coverage and resolution.** 96 data centers in 12 countries. Timeline file:
575 dated records, December 2018 to January 2030. Unit of observation: one
site (data_centers.csv) or one site on one date (data_center_timelines.csv).

**Licence.** Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0).

**Access.** Downloaded as a ZIP of seven CSV files plus a README from the Epoch AI data centers downloads page (https://epoch.ai/data/data-centers-documentation/downloads). Can be downloaded from Epoch AI's website for future use though it may differ from the file used here.

**Known problems.** A few problems are:-
-20 sites show 0 MW current power (likely planned or under construction).
-Only 28 timeline records come from before 2023.
-Capacity is not consumption (Epoch: typically 60-80% of capacity).

```{r source-1-load}
# Raw files as received.
epoch_sites    <- read_csv("data/raw/epoch_data_centers/data_centers.csv")
epoch_timeline <- read_csv("data/raw/epoch_data_centers/data_center_timelines.csv")

# Shape of each file.
glimpse(epoch_sites)
glimpse(epoch_timeline)

```

## 2.2.2 Statistics Canada Table 36-10-0434-01, GDP by industry

**Producer and authority.** Statistics Canada is Canada's national statistical agency, which
collects and publishes data under the Statistics Act. Statistics Canada is committed to transparency and accountability by providing access to its information in response to access to information or privacy requests where permitted by law.

**Original Dataset Purpose.** Part of Canada's national accounts; measures monthly economic
output (GDP at basic prices) of each industry, used to track the economy.

**Collection method.** Data are extracted from administrative files and derived from other Statistics Canada surveys and other sources.

**Coverage and resolution.** Canada only

**Licence.** Statistics Canada Open Licence.

**Access.** Downloaded as a full-table CSV (data file plus metadata file) from https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=3610043401. Can be downloaded for future use to study the year used.

**Known problems.** long format with several rows per month per industry (seasonal
adjustment and price types). Industry list is broader than the AI survey's sectors

```{r source-2-load}
# Raw file as received.
statcan_gdp <- read_csv("data/raw/statcan_GDP/36100434.csv")

glimpse(statcan_gdp)
```

## 2.2.3: Statistics Canada Table 33-10-1167-01, AI use by industry

**Producer and authority.**  Statistics Canada, under the Statistics Act, through the Canadian
Survey on Business Conditions.

**Original Dataset Purpose.** The survey tracks the environment businesses operate in and their
expectations

**Collection method.** Collected through online questionnaire. Self-reported:
businesses may define "using AI" differently

**Coverage and resolution.** Covers Canada. 20 AI-use categories (Yes, No, 18 application types). Values are percent of businesses.

**Licence.** Statistics Canada Open Licence.

**Access.** Downloaded as a full-table CSV (data file plus metadata file) from https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=3310116701.

**Known problems.** Survey excludes some industries in the GDP table and lots of missing values.

```{r source-3-load}
statcan_ai <- read_csv("data/raw/statcan_AI_use_by_industry/33101167.csv")

glimpse(statcan_ai)
```
## 2.3: Investigated and rejected sources

- Epoch AI Models: Training energy available for few models, falling to 30 in 2025 and 3 in 2026 because companies stopped disclosing and covers training only, not running models.

-LBNL 2024 report: Published as PDF tables, covers all data centers(not only AI), and no licence statement found.

-SEC EDGAR: company revenue for all US public companies, but quarterly files are large.

-StatCan Table 33-10-1045-01: measures planned AI use over the next 12 months, not actual use.

## 2.4: What I could not find

Could not find a Canadian or government dataset of AI data center electricity use. Later found out that companies such as Google, Microsoft and xAI do not publish per-site electricity consumption. Statistics Can also has no data center electricity table.

## 3.3: Downstream permissions

All of the data used in this project is open data. The code in this repository is covered by the MIT licence included in the repo, so anyone can reuse or modify it. Both licences(CC BY 4.0 and Statistics Canada Open Licence) allow the data to be used, modified and shared, as long as the original source is credited. Anyone reusing this project's data must credit Epoch AI and Statistics Canada as the original sources, as well as this project.

# 4: Consent and identifiability

None of the data used in this project describes individual people. EpochAI describes facilities and the companies that own them, StatCan GDP is industry totals and the AI table reports weighted percentages of businesses. However the raw AI table also contains rows by majority ownership group(First Nations, Métis or Inuit).

**Consent.** Built from from satellite imagery, companies that own them permits EpochAI so no individuals were asked to provide information. The two Statistics Canada tables come from surveys of businesses, collected under the Statistics Act.

**Identifiability.** None of the data I analyze describes individual people. Some of the provincial groups used in GDP data are very small which is why Statistics Canada has marked many of those cells as too unreliable to publish or left them blank.

**How sensitive data will be used.** I will keep the raw AI-use file unchanged, exactly as Statistics Canada published it, but my code will filter it to national industry rows only. My cleaned dataset and results will not include any breakdowns by province or by ownership group.

---

# 5: Exclusions and harms

## 5.1: Excluded data from the audit

Data that will not be used: Columns dropped from Epoch data (Investors, Construction companies, Energy
companies, Project, mostly blank) as they describe who funded or built each site, which has nothing to do with the question about power use. Statistic Can AI rows by ownership group will not be used as question compares industries, not types of business owners. The four Epoch files not used (chip types, chip quantities, chillers, cooling towers) as they describe computing hardware (which chips and how many) not resource use. As our cost side is power, which the timelines file already gives.

## 5.2: Who could be harmed

Communities near the data centers as the data is collected from satellite images.

## 5.3: Unreleased working data

I do not have any working data that I would keep unpublished.
